what: Local before/after cost of ADR-017 spatial aggregation, on synthetic geometry.
tier: CI regression tier (landsat_lst.benchmarks). Not a production measurement.
method: landsat_lst.benchmarks.measure, one fresh subprocess per configuration, peak RSS from /proc/self/status VmHWM. The two arms differ only in Geometry.aggregate.
findings: The source read is unchanged: 1.00 native passes in every arm. Aggregation reduces the output, never the bytes fetched and decoded.
The offset graph is identical on both grids (2,668 tasks). The estimator does not move when the output grid moves.
Composite task count RISES: 2.53x at 24 scenes, 3.25x at 60, 3.96x at 120. Three coarsen reductions over the full stack account for it.

Peak RSS falls, and the saving grows with scene depth: 0.90x at 24 scenes, 0.79x at 60, 0.67x at 120. The scene-dependent term is the single-time-chunk rechunk, which is nine times smaller on the delivered grid; the flat terms are not.
Wall time rises at this geometry (0.64 to 0.93 s at 24 scenes). Nothing streams at 1,026 squared, so the added reduction is pure cost here. It is not evidence about a production tile either way.
not_measured: End-to-end wall time for a tile, on either grid. No figure is claimed.
Peak RSS at production geometry (18,000 squared, ~2,930 scenes). Only a VM reports a peak; see docs/findings-memory-model.md.

R_COMPOSITE_MB_S after the change. It is an END-TO-END COMPOSITE rate with the percentile inside it, not an I/O rate, so ADR-017 makes it stale rather than still valid. Its percentile share cannot be backed out of the existing probe: the 45.5 MB/s arm ran on a 4.4%-land tile whose ocean nodata deflated ~8x on the wire.
Output size on a real tile after COG compression. The projection reports 0.50 GB uncompressed against 4.54 GB, an exact 9x, which is arithmetic rather than a measurement.

percentile_microbenchmark.what: nanquantile_last alone, the dominant composite compute, at equal scene depth.
percentile_microbenchmark.method: numpy only, outside dask, random float32 with 30% NaN, median of 5 runs.
percentile_microbenchmark.caveat: One kernel in isolation on synthetic data. What share of a tile's wall clock it holds is unmeasured, so this does not convert into a tile speedup.

wall_time_note: The wall_s column in `rows` is NOT evidence about production speed. In this harness the source is da.random.integers over the full source-grid stack, which runs identically in both arms and dominates a 1,026 squared run; the percentile is too small to register. Read those rows for task count and peak RSS only.
